# Skill writing guidance

Describe what the skill does and when it applies. Keep the trigger specific enough to avoid unrelated work. Separate the reusable procedure from the example that motivated it.

Keep essential decisions and constraints in SKILL.md; link focused references for conditional details. Scripts are useful for deterministic repeated operations, but should be tested without live side effects first.

Honor the user's chosen tools, scope, and prior authorization. Do not use skill installation as permission for deployment, payments, public sharing, or reading unrelated conversations. Skills guide an agent; they do not supply hidden memory or always-on execution.

Validate the frontmatter, relative links, examples, and behavior on representative requests. A skill for creating Grep agents must distinguish local instruction files from the remote agent lifecycle.
